final_proof:
Let us recall explicitly the relevant morphism conditions. An object of the comma category \((\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}\downarrow F)\) is a triple \((E,*,g)\), where \(E\) is an object of \(\mathbf C\) and
\[
g:\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}(E)=E\longrightarrow F(*)=C
\]
is a morphism in \(\mathbf C\). Thus \(g:E\to C\) is indeed an object of the slice category \(\mathbf C/C\), so the stated object assignment of \(J\) is well-defined.

Suppose
\[
(k,\operatorname{id}_*):(E,*,g)\longrightarrow(E',*,g')
\]
is a morphism in the comma category. (The second component must be \(\operatorname{id}_*\), since \(\mathbf 1\) has only that morphism.) By the defining commutativity condition for a comma morphism,
\[
F(\operatorname{id}_*)\circ g=g'\circ\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}(k).
\]
Because \(F(\operatorname{id}_*)=\operatorname{id}_C\) and \(\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}(k)=k\), this condition is exactly
\[
g'\circ k=g.
\]
That is precisely the condition saying that \(k:E\to E'\) is a morphism from \(g:E\to C\) to \(g':E'\to C\) in \(\mathbf C/C\). Hence the stated morphism assignment of \(J\) is also well-defined.

It remains to verify the functor axioms. The identity morphism of \((E,*,g)\) in the comma category is \((\operatorname{id}_E,\operatorname{id}_*)\). Therefore
\[
J(\operatorname{id}_E,\operatorname{id}_*)=\operatorname{id}_E,
\]
which is the identity morphism of the slice object \(g:E\to C\).

Now let
\[
(k,\operatorname{id}_*):(E,*,g)\to(E',*,g')
\quad\text{and}\quad
(\ell,\operatorname{id}_*):(E',*,g')\to(E'',*,g'')
\]
be composable comma morphisms. Their composite is \((\ell\circ k,\operatorname{id}_*)\), and consequently
\[
J\bigl((\ell,\operatorname{id}_*)\circ(k,\operatorname{id}_*)\bigr)
=J(\ell\circ k,\operatorname{id}_*)
=\ell\circ k
=J(\ell,\operatorname{id}_*)\circ J(k,\operatorname{id}_*).
\]
Thus \(J\) preserves identities and composition. Since it also assigns each object and morphism to an object and morphism of the indicated target category, \(J\) is a covariant functor \((\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf C}\downarrow F)\to\mathbf C/C\).
